358: | Code | Condition | Action |
359: |------|-----------|--------|

361: | `SYSTEMD_ON_WINDOWS` | systemd on Windows host | Refuse; choose WindowsService or other |
362: | `WINDOWS_SERVICE_ON_LINUX` | WindowsService on Linux | Refuse; choose linux-publish-swap or other |
363: | `SYSTEMD_PENDING_VALIDATION` | systemd selected as primary | Refuse/redirect until a tested unit exists; use linux-publish-swap or other |
364: | `MISSING_PLUGIN_ROOT` | Agent selected, no plugin path and clone denied | Stop configure until plugin available |
365: | `AGENT_FAMILY_UNSUPPORTED` | Cursor/other without operator-owned procedure | Stop or remove family |
366: | `AGENT_PLAYBOOK_UNVERIFIED` | Cowork/OpenCode activation unclear | Stop, redirect, or remove |
367: | `STORAGE_PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED` | Chosen storage not in this build | Stop; switch storage or build |

57: ## Architecture
58: 
59: **McpServer** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:
60: 
61: - **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/mcpserver/*`).
62: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
63: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.
64: 
65: **Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.
66: 
67: **Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.
68: 
69: **Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.
70: 
71: **Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.

Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.

81: All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). Use the layer catalog surface (`workflow.requirements.listLayers/createLayer/updateLayer`, `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync/CreateRequirementLayerAsync/UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`, `req_list_layers/req_create_layer/req_update_layer`, or equivalent plugin tools) when the user asks to inspect or manage requirement layers. Do not treat raw all-requirements lists, exported markdown, or future-layer requirements as currently enforceable unless the user explicitly asks to inspect or plan those layers.
212:   ## YAML Mutation Rule
213: 
214:   - Never edit YAML files by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. This includes one-key configuration changes.
215: 
216:   - Always deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save the serialized result.

224:   - If the MCP Server or required-plugin failure reveals that code, docs, requirements, plugin skills, package sync, deployment, configuration, or other artifacts need to be updated as a separate repair workflow, write a detailed triage report that includes the needed changes, acceptance criteria, and validation evidence, then continue the active task after the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds.
225:   - If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Keep the failsafe YAML report for later replay; do not use raw REST or another reporting channel as a substitute.

227:   ## Agent Help (MCP Server issues)

REST: `POST /mcpserver/agent-help/session` then WebSocket `/mcpserver/agent-help/session/{id}/stream` (SSE fallback: `POST .../turn/stream`).

232:   - Agent help is for diagnosis and coordination, not a substitute for the required plugin route for normal MCP work.

234:   ## MCP Memories
235:   MCP memories are durable operator guidance managed by the MCP Server. Global memories apply to every workspace; Workspace memories apply only to the active workspace. Memory IDs use `MEMORY-{CATEGORY}-{NNN}`.
236:   Agents that support request-boundary injection must render required memories exactly as:

238:   If no required memories are visible, render:

240:   Preserve raw memory text exactly; do not summarize, paraphrase, reorder within a scope, silently generate new memories, or add secrets. MCP memories are not a secret store. Effective memory order is Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID.

282:   The workspace API key rotates on every server restart, so an in-flight agent will begin seeing 401 on /mcpserver/* calls. When that happens, resume through your required agent plugin - do not hand-roll raw REST for session, TODO, or requirements work:

287:   5. Recover the open turn instead of starting over: query session history through the plugin (workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory), find the in-progress turn, then keep updating and complete it via the plugin. Do not open a duplicate session for the same work.

Re-check the workspace current directory, explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and plugin cache/session state through the wrapper; do not use raw REST merely because history is empty or marked deprecated.
289:   6. If the plugin cannot re-establish trust after the restart, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>` and continue with non-MCP local diagnosis only.

NAME
    Update-LinesInFile
    
SYNOPSIS
    Replace or delete specific lines in a text file
    
    
SYNTAX
    Update-LinesInFile [-Path] <string[]> [[-Content] <Object[]>] [-LineRange <string[]>] [-Skip <int>] [-First <int>] [-Encoding <string>] [-Backup] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Update-LinesInFile [[-Content] <Object[]>] -LiteralPath <string[]> [-LineRange <string[]>] [-Skip <int>] [-First <int>] [-Encoding <string>] [-Backup] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Replaces specified line range with new content.
    Lines can expand or shrink.
    
    Update-LinesInFile file.txt -LineRange 5 -Content "replaced"           # replace line 5
    
    Update-LinesInFile file.txt -LineRange 5,10 -Content "single line"     # replace 6 lines with 1
    
    Update-LinesInFile file.txt -LineRange 5,10 -Content @()               # delete lines 5-10
    
    Update-LinesInFile file.txt -Content @("line1", "line2")               # replace entire file
    

PARAMETERS
    -Backup
        Creates a backup file before modifying.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      none
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Confirm
        Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      cf
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Encoding <System.String>
        Character encoding.
        Auto-detected if omitted.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      none
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -First <System.Nullable`1[System.Int32]>
        Number of lines to process.
        Use with `-Skip` to define a range, or alone to process from the beginning.
        Mapped to `-LineRange` internally (e.g., `-First 20` becomes `-LineRange 1-20`).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      none
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -LineRange <System.String[]>
        Line range to replace.
        Accepts: `5` (single line), `5,10` (range), `5-10` (dash format).
        Omit to replace entire file.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      none
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Path <System.String[]>
        File path(s).
        Supports wildcards.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByPropertyName)
        Aliases                      none
        Accept wildcard characters?  true
        
    -Skip <System.Nullable`1[System.Int32]>
        Number of lines to skip from the beginning.
        Use with `-First` to define a window (e.g., `-Skip 200 -First 50` becomes `-LineRange 201-250`).
        Use alone to skip lines and process to end of file (e.g., `-Skip 100` becomes `-LineRange 101,-1`).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      none
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -WhatIf
        Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    Named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Aliases                      wi

        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see
        about_CommonParameters (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    System.String[]
        File path(s) to process.
    
    System.Object[]
        File path(s) to process.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
NOTES
    
    
        - `-Content @()` deletes lines (empty array).
        
        - Omitting `-LineRange` replaces entire file.
        
        - To pass content containing `$`, backticks, or quotes, use the `var1` parameter of `execute_command`: `Update-LinesInFile path -LineRange 5 -Content $var1`
    
    --------- Basic usage ---------
    
    Update-LinesInFile file.txt -LineRange 5 -Content "replaced"
    Update-LinesInFile file.txt -LineRange 5,10 -Content @()

TodoEvidence.Title: Setup prompt for obtaining, installing, and configuring MCP Server by a frontier agent
Description: Deliver a reusable frontier-agent setup prompt (and supporting checklist) that obtains, installs, and configures MCP Server so a fresh agent can reach a verified working host without operator tribal knowledge.

The prompt MUST interactively gather environment specifics before acting: agents in use, development process (BDPv4 or user-owned process), storage backend (MSSQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite), and service installation target (Windows Service, systemd, or other).

The prompt MUST give concrete handling guidance for each intake scenario (and common combinations), not only ask questions: what to install, which plugin/identity path, how to wire storage, how to register the service, verify, and what to do on failure.

Session log is NOT available during setup. After intake, the agent MUST write (1) a setup choices manifest capturing answers and selected playbook IDs, and (2) an implementation plan derived from those choices, before performing obtain/install/configure. Later steps and verify read that manifest/plan, not a session log.
Scope: Windows lab host (PAYTON-LEGION2 pattern) first as a reference path; branch install/configure steps from the gathered answers. Document extension points for other hosts.
Out of scope for v1: production multi-tenant deploy, public publishing of add-profile/operator profile, and process-drift enforcement (MCP-PROCESS-001).
TechnicalDetails: Artifact target: docs prompt under mcpserver (or plugin docs) plus a copy-paste agent prompt block; prefer PowerShell-only steps where the host is Windows; note shell equivalents when target is systemd/other.
Interactive intake (required before obtain/install): (1) agents used; (2) process: BDPv4 vs custom; (3) storage: MSSQL | PostgreSQL | SQLite; (4) service target: Windows Service | systemd | other.

Scenario playbooks: per-agent (plugin/identity/skill/invoke); per-process (BDPv4 vs custom); per-storage (config/prereqs/bootstrap/smoke); per-service-target (install/start/stop/logs/health). Conflicts refuse or redirect with remediation.

Post-intake artifacts (required, no session log): setup-choices.manifest (YAML or JSON) with answers, playbook IDs, timestamp, host notes; setup-implementation.plan with ordered steps, branched commands, verify criteria, and stop conditions. Path convention documented in the prompt (e.g. under workspace docs/setup/ or operator-chosen path).
Obtain/install/configure/verify MUST load the manifest and follow the plan; verify asserts manifest fields match the live host and that plan steps were completed.
Invoke path after install: host-matched plugin via lib/repl-invoke.ps1 / skills/*/scripts/invoke.ps1; identity from manifest. Do not default to raw :7147 REST or broken box connectors.
Success = smoke type:result for sessionlog bootstrap, todo query, memory list/get against chosen storage/service, plus confirmation that verify matched the written manifest/plan.

ImplementationTasks.Task: Inventory current install surfaces: McpServer repo, NuGet/tooling, UpdateService, plugin repos (grok/codex), local skill mirrors under ~/.grok/skills
Design interactive intake questionnaire: agents, BDP vs own process, storage, service target; define required follow-up fields per answer
Write scenario playbooks: per-agent, per-process, per-storage, per-service-target handling guidance
Document conflict/unsupported combinations and stop/remediation guidance
Define setup-choices.manifest and setup-implementation.plan schemas, paths, and write/load rules (no session log dependency)
Write obtain/install/configure sections that load manifest and execute the plan
Write verify section that asserts live host matches manifest and plan completion criteria
Add frontier-agent prompt block: intake first, write manifest+plan, then execute; stop conditions and receipt format from those files
Add host matrix + non-goals; link MCP-PROCESS-001 without blocking v1 setup
Dry-run on Legion with at least two intake variants; confirm manifest/plan artifacts and verify; revise gaps

TodoEvidence.Title: Setup prompt for obtaining, installing, and configuring MCP Server by a frontier agent
Description: Deliver a reusable frontier-agent setup prompt (and supporting checklist) that obtains, installs, and configures MCP Server so a fresh agent can reach a verified working host without operator tribal knowledge.

The prompt MUST interactively gather environment specifics before acting: agents in use, development process (BDPv4 or user-owned process), storage backend (MSSQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite), and service installation target (Windows Service, systemd, or other).

The prompt MUST give concrete handling guidance for each intake scenario (and common combinations), not only ask questions: what to install, which plugin/identity path, how to wire storage, how to register the service, verify, and what to do on failure.

Session log is NOT available during setup. After intake, the agent MUST write (1) a setup choices manifest capturing answers and selected playbook IDs, and (2) an implementation plan derived from those choices, before performing obtain/install/configure. Later steps and verify read that manifest/plan, not a session log.
Scope: Windows lab host (PAYTON-LEGION2 pattern) first as a reference path; branch install/configure steps from the gathered answers. Document extension points for other hosts.
Out of scope for v1: production multi-tenant deploy, public publishing of add-profile/operator profile, and process-drift enforcement (MCP-PROCESS-001).
TechnicalDetails: Artifact target: docs prompt under mcpserver (or plugin docs) plus a copy-paste agent prompt block; prefer PowerShell-only steps where the host is Windows; note shell equivalents when target is systemd/other.
Interactive intake (required before obtain/install): (1) agents used; (2) process: BDPv4 vs custom; (3) storage: MSSQL | PostgreSQL | SQLite; (4) service target: Windows Service | systemd | other.

Scenario playbooks: per-agent (plugin/identity/skill/invoke); per-process (BDPv4 vs custom); per-storage (config/prereqs/bootstrap/smoke); per-service-target (install/start/stop/logs/health). Conflicts refuse or redirect with remediation.

Post-intake artifacts (required, no session log): setup-choices.manifest (YAML or JSON) with answers, playbook IDs, timestamp, host notes; setup-implementation.plan with ordered steps, branched commands, verify criteria, and stop conditions. Path convention documented in the prompt (e.g. under workspace docs/setup/ or operator-chosen path).
Obtain/install/configure/verify MUST load the manifest and follow the plan; verify asserts manifest fields match the live host and that plan steps were completed.
Invoke path after install: host-matched plugin via lib/repl-invoke.ps1 / skills/*/scripts/invoke.ps1; identity from manifest. Do not default to raw :7147 REST or broken box connectors.
Success = smoke type:result for sessionlog bootstrap, todo query, memory list/get against chosen storage/service, plus confirmation that verify matched the written manifest/plan.
